learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the collapse of the Soviet Union, the end of the Cold War era, and the dramatic transition of communist countries to capitalism!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An economic and political system based on socialist principles where the state controlled all property and the economy, led by a single party (the Communist Party) with no room for opposition.

Mikhail Gorbachev introduced economic and political reforms (Perestroika and Glasnost). However, these changes inadvertently triggered nationalist movements, leading to the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991.
The painful and sudden transition of post-communist countries from an authoritarian socialist system to a democratic capitalist system, directed by the World Bank and IMF.
It led to economic ruin in Russia. State-controlled industries were sold at throwaway prices (the largest garage sale in history), inflation soared, and the social welfare system was dismantled.
India maintained warm, strategic relations with all post-communist countries, especially Russia, sharing a vision of a multipolar world order.

fun_activity.title: 🗺️ Map the Breakup
fun_activity.instructions: Find a map of the Soviet Union from 1989 and compare it with a modern map of Asia and Europe. Try to identify the 15 new independent nations that were born from the single Soviet empire!

exam_tips: 📌 Always explain 'Shock Therapy' along with its negative economic consequences in Russia, such as the 'largest garage sale in history'.
📌 Clearly outline Mikhail Gorbachev’s twin policies: Glasnost (openness) and Perestroika (restructuring).
📌 Remember that the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 marked the symbolic end of the Cold War.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Soviet Union (USSR) disintegrated into 15 independent republics in 1991.
⭐ Shock Therapy was the painful transition from socialism to capitalism managed by the IMF and World Bank.
⭐ A unipolar world emerged temporarily under US dominance after the end of bipolarity.
